title: Temporal tenant throttling and burst sandbox for Dedicated capacity
creator: Priya N. Desai
description: PRD: introduce a Temporal Tenant Throttling feature and a configurable Burst Sandbox window for Dedicated capacity. This feature lets tenants consume short-duration excess capacity within controlled time windows while preserving long-term isolation guarantees for reserved pools. The goal is to provide predictable, observable burst behavior that cooperates with autoscaling and preemption policies.
background: Customers running on Dedicated pools have asked for safer, auditable burst behavior: they want predictable short bursts for traffic spikes without risking noisy-neighbor effects on other reserved tenants. Existing reserved pools + soft-evict logic is conservative and either blocks bursts or preempts too aggressively. We need an orthogonal mechanism that defines temporal burst windows, per-tenant caps inside those windows, and shaping rules so autoscalers and the scheduler can reason about transient demand.
problem_statement: Without a temporal burst mechanism, tenants either over-provision (waste cost) or get throttled during spikes (poor UX). Current soft-evict and spill mechanisms are reactive and opaque in billing and telemetry. We need a configurable, observable policy that: 1) allows controlled short bursts, 2) prevents unbounded work stealing from other tenants, and 3) integrates with autoscaling and billing.
goals: Define a burst sandbox concept: time-windowed allowance per tenant that permits limited excess usage without violating isolation SLOs
Expose simple UI and API controls for per-tenant temporal windows and per-window caps
Ensure autoscaler and scheduler honor sandbox budgets and prefer prewarming over disruptive preemption
Provide telemetry, alerts, and billing labels so customers and Redwood can audit burst usage
Ship a canary rollout in a single region with telemetry hooks and automated rollback criteria
out_of_scope: Replacing long-term reserved capacity or hard quota semantics
Multi-region redistribution of reserved pools as part of this feature
Detailed invoicing changes beyond labeling usage and exposing burst metrics
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-initiated reserve-ups for short spikes by >= 30% within 90 days
Less than 3% increase in overall 95th percentile latency for non-burst tenants in the same pool during canary
Burst-related customer complaints drop or are classified as feature questions rather than incidents
Telemetry shows >= 80% of bursts completed without triggering cross-tenant preemption in pilot pools
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to configure a 5-minute burst window with a 2x compute multiplier for tenant A so short spikes are absorbed without manual reserve changes
As a customer, I want to see a dashboard line item that shows burst budget remaining in current window so I can judge whether to rely on bursts or scale capacity
As an SRE, I want burst usage labeled in traces and billing exports so I can correlate latency regressions with burst events
As an autoscaler, I want predictive signals about nearing burst budget exhaustion so I can decide to prewarm nodes instead of draining others
acceptance_criteria: API: New PATCH /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/burst-config supports fields: window_seconds, multiplier, cap_tokens, preemption_behavior, enabled; returns 200 and persisted config
Console: Tenant settings page exposes burst config with validation and an explanatory tooltip; changes are auditable in change log
Runtime: Scheduler will honor burst budgets and enforce per-window caps; when cap exceeded, additional requests are rejected with 429 and a clear reason code 'BURST_CAP_EXCEEDED'
Autoscaler integration: Autoscaler receives a signal when remaining burst budget <= 20% and can trigger prewarm policy without immediate eviction
Telemetry: Burst events generate a labeled metric (dedicated.burst.usage) and trace annotation; billing export includes burst.label with token counts
Canary: Feature toggled via config per-cluster; pilot region shows no >3% tail-latency regression for unrelated tenants over a 7-day window
Tests: E2E test harness simulates spike workload, verifies cap enforcement, and validates non-burst tenants' latency remains within SLO
requirements: Config model persisted in control-plane with validation and RBAC (admins can set, tenant-admins can request/override depending on entitlement)
Runtime accounting: lightweight per-tenant, per-window token bucket tracked in scheduler/process with periodic checkpointing to prevent drift
Metrics: emit per-tenant metrics with granularity <= 1m for burst usage, rejections, and preemption events
API & Console: UI preview of expected billing impact for a sample workload given the burst multiplier and cap
Fallback: when control-plane connectivity fails, runtime must default to safe behavior (disabled or conservative cap)
Auditability: all config changes produce an audit log entry with user, timestamp, and diff
design_considerations: Token model vs. simple rate multiplier: token model chosen to allow fine-grained caps and easier billing attribution
Window semantics: strictly sliding windows are more complex; initial implementation uses fixed-length aligned windows per-tenant with a plan to iterate to sliding if needed
Scheduler implications: soft enforcement with preferential throttling vs. hard preemption; default is soft (reject or queue) with tenant-configurable preemption_behavior
Interaction with reserved pools: burst budgets are charged to tenant and limited to pool headroom; the scheduler must never reassign nodes that would violate other tenants' reservations
Performance: accounting must be O(1) per request and negligible per-token overhead; favor in-memory counters with periodic durable snapshots
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal alpha): enable feature for Redwood-owned test tenants in a single pilot cluster; run synthetic spike tests; collect metrics
Phase 2 (Customer pilot): onboard 2-3 customers with agreed SLAs; enable in single region; monitor 30 days
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout): enable opt-in via console for all Dedicated customers in region; telemetry guardrails trigger automatic throttling/rollback
Phase 4 (GA): enable UI, API, docs, and billing labels; run education email and update onboarding guides
risks: Noisy neighbor regressions if caps or enforcement are misconfigured; mitigated by canary and pool headroom requirement
Billing confusion if burst usage is not surfaced clearly; mitigation: UI preview and billing exports with labeled tokens
Scheduler complexity may increase, causing subtle bugs in eviction paths; mitigation: add invariant tests and a simulation harness
Cross-region skew: tenants with multi-region pools may see inconsistent burst behavior; put multi-region support in backlog
dependencies: ENG-20112: scheduler per-tenant accounting primitives (in flight)
ENG-21045: autoscaler prewarm hook and signal endpoint
ENG-23901: console settings UI components and audit log plumbing
Billing-ops: export label support for burst usage in billing pipeline
stakeholders: Engineering: Luca Moretti (PM-ENG lead), Mei Chen (Scheduler), Rafael Gomez (Autoscale)
